objective: Sequential focused-task campaign to improve validated learning efficiency and higher-order quantitative-research capability.
process_conclusion: Concrete selector advantage demonstrated at the level of information flow: after frontier-first adoption, six consecutive activations each selected a distinct highest-value unresolved frontier cell and closed it exactly once with a decisive verdict (5 FALSIFIED, 1 SUPPORTED) plus independent-verification MATCH and determinism, with zero equivalent re-tests and zero duplicated frontier cells. The documented pre-adoption condition shows the opposite pattern: opportunistic selection (37260572520) produced an UNVERIFIED process delta and the frontier was not operative. The advantage is real but bounded: it is confounded by concurrent toolkit maturation and the absence of a controlled counterfactual, and it is delivered through the frontier artifact rather than the selector in isolation.

The audit produced a concrete, evidence-backed duplicate-avoidance conclusion: the durable history prevents duplicate frontier-cell experiments (each resolved cell is recorded once with a terminal status, and agents 01-03 executed three distinct tasks with no equivalent re-test). The single near-duplicate found is a pre-campaign orphaned implementation (research/checks/momentum_sweep.py, no artifact, referenced nowhere) which is now explicitly annotated as superseded so a future agent will not re-run it as a new experiment. The minimal novelty guard (frontier table terminal statuses + Learning rule 2 + exact-task_id dedup) is judged SUFFICIENT for the current campaign; no controller/process mechanism change is warranted.
research_conclusion: MARKET/COST (research simulation, not live): the short-horizon momentum edge is COST_ROBUST on the collected 10-asset universe. Under the repository's existing realistic cost model and a 2x conservative stress, all 6 zero-cost lookback-robust assets (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA) retain a positive REGIME_STABLE edge (COST_ROBUST=6, DEGRADED=0, REJECTED=0); the per-fold transaction-cost drag is ~1e-5..1e-4 in log return, ~1000x below the ~0.05-0.13 edge magnitude. The a-priori prediction was confirmed. A documented methodological caveat: the framework's coin-flip null has ~60x the candidate's turnover and is far more cost-penalised, so the candidate-minus-null gap widens under costs and is not a valid cost-stress measure; the verdict is based on the candidate's own absolute medians. Independently verified (fresh walk_forward + noise_benchmark, cross-consistency vs the admitted lookback artifact, verdict reproducibility, determinism) and the full regression suite passes (168 tests).
unverified: No controlled counterfactual exists: the repository cannot rerun the pre-adoption regime under the new selector, so the selector's marginal causal contribution is not isolated.

The 'no equivalent re-tests' property is realized through the frontier artifact the selector selects from; the selector and the frontier table are coupled, so their individual contributions are not separable from durable evidence alone.

The audit covers the current campaign (3 agents) and the pre-campaign manual phase; it does not prove the guard would catch every future equivalent experiment, only that none has occurred so far at the frontier-cell level.

The controller has no semantic (near-duplicate) novelty enforcement; duplicate prevention relies on the frontier table plus agent discipline. This has held for agents 01-03 but is not deterministically enforced, so a future near-duplicate task phrasing could still be selected.

The engine sizes positions constant-dollar and rebalances every bar, so turnover (and hence the cost drag) is driven by that mechanical rebalance; a signal-change-only rebalance implementation would have lower turnover and is not tested here (changing it would be a methodology change, out of scope).

The framework's matched null (random_signals, 3-state) has much higher turnover than the candidate, so the candidate-minus-null gap widens under costs; this is a documented null-turnover asymmetry, not a symmetric stress, and the cost-robustness verdict deliberately does not rely on that gap.

The improvement coincides with concurrent infrastructure maturation (toolkit built 2026-10-02..10-04; bash execution available from 37263008074), so part of the observed information-flow gain may be attributable to tooling maturity rather than the selector alone.

The pre-adoption research-selection sample is effectively n=1 (only 37260572520 is a clearly opportunistic research-cell selection); earlier activations were infrastructure/roadmap work, so the 'before' condition is thin.

The repository's 'realistic' cost model is a single fixed parameterisation (commission_per_trade=2.0, commission_per_share=0.003, slippage_cents=2.0, slippage_proportional=0.0005); the 2x conservative level is a bounded stress, not an exhaustive sweep of market-impact/liquidity regimes, so the result is conditional on that cost family.

The result is exploratory research simulation on one collected 10-asset universe (2009-2026); it is not evidence of live profitability and does not establish that the edge survives real-world market impact beyond the modelled costs.

Whether research/checks/momentum_sweep.py was ever executed is unknown (no artifact, no log reference); it is treated as superseded/redundant, not as a validated negative result, and its unrun status is not claimed either way.
